mainTopic: The holy area of the עזרה and its chambers, the 'opposite the entrance' rule, and blood becoming פסול at sunset
overview: The amud opens with the size of the עזרה: 187 by 135 אמות. רב נחמן teaches that inside this area כהנים eat קדשי קדשים and slaughter קדשים קלים, and anyone who enters it while טמא is liable. The גמרא asks what the exact numbers leave out. It is not the windows or the thickness of the wall, so it must be the לשכות, the chambers built outside but opening into the courtyard. A ברייתא shows that by Torah law קדשי קדשים may be eaten in those chambers, so רבא explains that eating is a special case. For slaughter and for entering while טמא, the chambers are not holy, and the גמרא corrects another ברייתא to read 'אין חייבין'. רבינא then shows that only slaughter, not eating, must be opposite the entrance, and the פסוק about the מילואים was a one-time rule. Finally רב יצחק בר אבודימי teaches that blood becomes פסול at sunset. The challenge to his source continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The size of the courtyard area
steps.stepSummary: The previous statement ends by giving the area's measurements: 187 אמות long by 135 wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: An area 187 long by 135 wide.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the tail end of a statement that began on the previous amud. It gives the size of the area being discussed: 187 by 135 אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two numbers are the measurements of the whole עזרה. The rest of the section depends on them. The גמרא will soon ask why such exact numbers are given, and what they come to leave out.

keyTerms.meaning: Length
Width
A cubit, the unit of measure (the numbers here are in אמות)

phrases.english: a length of 187
phrases.notes: The numbers are in אמות (cubits), even though the word isn't written.

phrases.english: by a width of 135.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a statement that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The area in question measures 187 by 135 אמות.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives the courtyard's size
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites before רב נחמן that the whole עזרה was 187 by 135 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רב נחמן: the whole courtyard was 187 by 135 wide.
steps.whatsHappening: A teacher whose job was to recite ברייתות says before רב נחמן that the whole עזרה measured 187 by 135 אמות. This sets up רב נחמן's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states the measurements as a plain fact about the Temple. It doesn't say what follows in הלכה from these numbers. רב נחמן is about to supply that.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, a reciter who memorized and recited ברייתות in the בית מדרש
The Temple courtyard
Before him, in his presence

phrases.english: A tanna taught before Rav Nachman:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָעֲזָרָה הָיְתָה מֵאָה שְׁמוֹנִים וָשֶׁבַע
phrases.english: The entire courtyard was 187
by a width of 135.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A ברייתא with the same measurements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The whole עזרה measured 187 by 135 אמות.

steps.title: רב נחמן: what happens inside that area
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes his father: inside an area like this, כהנים eat קדשי קדשים, slaughter קדשים קלים, and are liable for entering in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what my father told me: in an area like this, the priests enter there and eat the most holy offerings there, and slaughter the lesser holy offerings there, and are liable for entering while impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן tells the תנא what his father taught him about this measured area. He lists three הלכות that apply exactly inside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns a bare measurement into a legal boundary. Inside the 187 by 135 area, קדשי קדשים may be eaten and קדשים קלים may be slaughtered. Someone who enters it while טמא is liable. So the measurement now marks exactly where the holy area begins and ends.

keyTerms.meaning: The most holy offerings, eaten only by כהנים inside the עזרה
Offerings of lesser holiness, which must be slaughtered in the עזרה
Liable for entering the holy area while ritually impure
In something like this (an area of these measurements)

steps.whyThisMatters: These measurements become the test for three separate הלכות, so it matters exactly which parts of the Temple fall inside them.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר לִי אַבָּא:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what my father said to me:
In an area such as this, priests enter there
and eat offerings of the most sacred order there,
and slaughter offerings of lesser sanctity there,
and are liable due to ritual impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר לִי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the legal meaning of the measurements from the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The area of 187 by 135 is where קדשי קדשים are eaten, קדשים קלים are slaughtered, and entering in טומאה makes one liable.

steps.title: What do the exact numbers leave out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what these precise measurements come to exclude.
steps.simpleTranslation: To exclude what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why such exact numbers were given. What part of the Temple falls outside them? This question sets up the next few steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an area is defined this precisely, something nearby must be left outside it. The גמרא wants to know what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to leave something out
What

phrases.english: To exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of רב נחמן's exact measurements.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which part of the Temple area do the exact measurements leave out?

steps.title: Not the windows and the wall's thickness
steps.stepSummary: Suggestion: the numbers leave out the windows, doors and thickness of the wall. Rejected, because a משנה rules that the windows and the wall's thickness count as inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is to exclude the windows, doors and the thickness of the wall, we learned: the windows and the thickness of the wall are like inside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one answer: the numbers leave out the windows, doors and walls. It rejects this right away by quoting a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (פסחים 85b) says the windows and the thickness of the wall count as inside the עזרה. So the measurement cannot be there to leave them out. The גמרא needs a different answer.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion that will be rejected)
The thickness of the wall
Like inside

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא לְמַעוֹטֵי חַלּוֹנוֹת, דְּלָתוֹת וְעוֹבִי הַחוֹמָה –
phrases.english: If we say it is to exclude windows, doors and the thickness of the wall,
we learned:
The windows and the thickness of the wall are as inside!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question and knocks it down.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the numbers exclude the windows and the wall's thickness.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A משנה explicitly counts the windows and the wall's thickness as inside the עזרה.

steps.title: Rather, the numbers leave out the chambers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes instead that the measurements exclude the לשכות, the chambers around the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is to exclude the chambers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer: the exact numbers leave out the chambers. The next step will question this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chambers were rooms built along the courtyard. The idea is that they fall outside the measured area, so the three הלכות of רב נחמן would not apply in them.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather (moving to a new answer)
Chambers, rooms around the courtyard

phrases.english: But rather, it is to exclude the chambers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer from step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The measurements come to exclude the chambers.

steps.title: But chambers opening into the holy area are holy
steps.stepSummary: Challenge: chambers built in the non-holy area but opening into the holy area are holy inside, according to a משנה. How can the measurement leave them out?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they are built in the non-holy area and open to the holy area, didn't we learn: their inside is holy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new answer. A משנה says some chambers are holy inside, so it seems they should not be excluded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in מעשר שני (3:8) rules that chambers built in a חול area but opening into the holy area are holy inside. Such chambers lie outside the measured 187 by 135. Yet the משנה treats them as holy, which seems to contradict excluding them.

keyTerms.meaning: Built in the non-holy area
Opening into the holy area
Their inside

phrases.english: And if they are built in the non-sacred area and open to the sacred area,
but didn't we learn: their inside is sacred!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the measurements exclude the chambers.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה rules that chambers built outside but opening into the holy area are holy inside, so it seems they cannot be excluded.

steps.title: Their holiness is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: Answer: the holiness of those chambers is only מדרבנן. So the measurement can still exclude them on the level of Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: By rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in one word. The holiness the משנה gives those chambers is only מדרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in מעשר שני speaks of holiness created by the חכמים. By Torah law those chambers are outside the holy area. So רב נחמן's measurement can leave them out, and the answer of step 6 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law, not by Torah law

steps.whatToRemember: The 187 by 135 measurement marks the עזרה as it is under Torah law. The windows and the wall's thickness count as inside. Chambers built outside but opening into the courtyard are excluded, because their holiness is only מדרבנן. Steps 9 and 10 refine this: by Torah law the chambers are holy for eating, but not for other laws.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the משנה in מעשר שני was rejected. Its ruling stands; the גמרא only explains that the holiness it describes is מדרבנן, not from the Torah.

phrases.english: By rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing levels of law (rabbinic vs. Torah)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Chambers that the משנה calls holy must be part of the holy area, so the measurement cannot exclude them.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their holiness is only מדרבנן. By Torah law they are outside the measured area and are excluded.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: At this stage, the exact measurements exclude the chambers, whose holiness is only מדרבנן. Step 10 refines this: by Torah law they are holy for eating only.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the chambers are holy by Torah law for eating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that the chambers are only holy מדרבנן. A ברייתא learns from a פסוק that כהנים may eat קדשי קדשים and שירי מנחה in those chambers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they really not holy by Torah law? A ברייתא teaches: how do we know that כהנים may go into chambers built in the non-holy area but opening into the holy area, and eat the holiest offerings and the leftover מנחה there? The פסוק says 'in the courtyard of the אהל מועד they shall eat it.' The Torah included many courtyards for this one kind of eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 8. It quotes a ברייתא showing that the Torah itself treats these chambers as holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said the chambers are holy only מדרבנן. But the ברייתא learns from a פסוק that the Torah allows eating קדשי קדשים there. That is a Torah-level law, so the chambers seem to be holy מדאורייתא after all.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law
The most holy offerings, which may only be eaten in the holy area
The leftover part of a flour offering, eaten by the כהנים
Included, widened (the Torah added more places)

phrases.english: And by Torah law they are not holy?!
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
Chambers built in the non-holy area,
and opening into the holy area.
From where do we know that the כהנים may enter there
and eat the most holy offerings there
and the leftovers of a flour offering?
The verse teaches:
"In the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting they shall eat it"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:9. The פסוק already said 'in a holy place,' so these extra words come to add more places.

phrases.english: The Torah included many courtyards
for one kind of eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 8 that the chambers are holy only מדרבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the holiness of the chambers is only מדרבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא derives from a פסוק that קדשי קדשים may be eaten in the chambers. That is a Torah-level holiness.

steps.title: רבא: eating is a special case
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the Torah included the chambers only for eating. For other laws they are not holy by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: eating is different.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. The Torah's extra holiness for these chambers covers eating alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in the ברייתא was about eating, so it only widens the eating area. For other laws, such as slaughtering קדשים קלים or the punishment for entering while impure, the chambers are not holy מדאורייתא. That way both step 8 and the ברייתא can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: Is different (a special case with its own rule)

phrases.english: רבא said:
Eating is different.
phrases.notes: He means the Torah added these chambers for eating only, not for other laws of the holy area.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope: the Torah's inclusion applies only to eating.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק makes the chambers fully holy by Torah law for every purpose.
steps.terutzMaskana: The chambers count as holy by Torah law only for eating. For other laws, their holiness is מדרבנן.

steps.title: A ברייתא says entering while impure brings liability
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's answer. A ברייתא says a person is liable for entering these chambers while impure, which sounds like full Torah holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for impurity, are they really not holy? A ברייתא teaches: in chambers built in the non-holy area and opening into the holy area, כהנים go in and eat the holiest offerings, but they may not slaughter קדשים קלים there. And a person is liable for entering there while impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא from a new angle. It quotes a ברייתא that seems to make a person liable for entering the chambers while impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the chambers are holy by Torah law only for eating. But this ברייתא says one is חייב for entering them while impure. That punishment (כרת) is a Torah-level law, so the chambers seem to be holy by Torah law for טומאה too.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual impurity; entering the holy area while impure brings כרת
Offerings of lesser holiness, which may be slaughtered anywhere in the עזרה
Are liable (to punishment)

phrases.english: But regarding impurity, they are not holy?!
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
Chambers that are built in the non-holy area
and open into the holy area —
כהנים enter there
and eat the most holy offerings there,
but they do not slaughter offerings of lesser holiness there,
and they are liable because of impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the chambers are holy by Torah law only for eating.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא makes one liable for entering the chambers while impure. That is a Torah punishment, so the chambers seem holy by Torah law for טומאה as well.

steps.title: Fix the ברייתא to say 'not liable'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא itself says one may not slaughter קדשים קלים there, so it treats the chambers as not holy for that law. To match, its wording should read that one is not liable for impurity either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't you say in that ברייתא 'they may not slaughter there'? Then also read it as 'they are not liable.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבא by correcting the wording of the ברייתא. It should say a person is NOT liable for entering while impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already admits the chambers are not holy for slaughtering קדשים קלים. So it agrees the chambers are holy only for eating. Its last line should match that and read 'אין חייבין', not liable, which fits רבא exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't you say? (points back to the ברייתא's own words)

phrases.english: Didn't you say "they do not slaughter"?
Teach also: "they are not liable."
phrases.notes: The גמרא is changing the ברייתא's wording here, so read its last line as 'not liable' for impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אָמְרַתְּ ״אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין״? תְּנִי נָמֵי ״אֵין חַיָּיבִין״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11, defending רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the ברייתא, using its own ruling on slaughtering.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא makes one liable for entering the chambers while impure, so they are holy by Torah law for טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא should read 'not liable.' It agrees that the chambers are holy by Torah law only for eating.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not changing the ברייתא for no reason. The ברייתא's own line, that one may not slaughter there, shows it treats the chambers as not fully holy. 'Not liable' simply matches that.
steps.whatToRemember: These chambers count as holy by Torah law only for eating קדשי קדשים, because the פסוק included them for that. For slaughtering קדשים קלים and for the punishment of entering while impure, they are not holy by Torah law.

steps.title: Maybe slaughter is forbidden there for a different reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the corrected wording from Step 12. Slaughter in the chambers may be forbidden only because it is not 'opposite the entrance.' If so, nothing forces us to say the chambers lack holiness, so why change the text to 'אין חייבין'?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, 'they may not slaughter' there, because slaughter must be opposite the entrance and here it is not. But why should 'they are not liable' be true?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the change of wording to 'אין חייבין.' It offers a different reason why slaughtering in the chambers is not allowed, a reason that has nothing to do with holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said: since the ברייתא forbids slaughtering קדשים קלים there, the chambers must not be holy. Now the גמרא says that rule may come from a separate requirement: slaughter must face the entrance (פתח אהל מועד), and a chamber does not. So the chambers could still be fully holy, and a person who enters them while impure would still be liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / this part makes sense
Opposite the entrance (of the היכל); required for slaughtering קדשים קלים
They may not slaughter
They are not liable (for entering while impure)

steps.confusionAlert: Slaughter being forbidden somewhere does not always mean the place is not holy. Here the גמרא suggests a separate reason, the 'opposite the entrance' rule.

phrases.english: Granted, 'they may not slaughter' there:
we need the slaughter to be opposite the entrance, and here it is not;
but 'they are not liable' — why?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning behind the correction made in Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The correction of the ברייתא from 'חייבין' to 'אין חייבין'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ban on slaughter can be explained by the 'opposite the entrance' rule, so it does not show the chambers lack holiness. That means there is no reason to change the liability clause.

steps.title: The case must be one where the chamber faces the entrance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא must be talking about slaughter that is opposite the entrance. Otherwise the rule would be too obvious to need teaching. So the real reason for the ban is that the chambers are not holy, and the ברייתא should also say 'אין חייבין.'
steps.simpleTranslation: By your logic, when it says 'they may not slaughter,' aren't we talking about slaughter that is opposite the entrance? If it weren't, why teach it at all? So even when he slaughters opposite the entrance, it says 'they may not slaughter' because the place is not holy. Then teach also 'they are not liable.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the corrected wording. It argues that the ברייתא must be discussing a chamber that does face the entrance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the chamber did not face the entrance, there would be nothing new in saying 'don't slaughter there,' since that is already known. A ruling only needs to be taught if it is teaching something. So the only reason left for the ban is that the chamber is not holy. That same lack of holiness means no liability for entering while impure.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning
Are we not dealing with (a case where)
Why was it necessary (to teach)?
Because it is not holy

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common גמרא tool: a ruling must teach something new, so we read it as covering the case where it adds something.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, 'they may not slaughter':
aren't we dealing
with a case where the slaughter is opposite the entrance?!
For if it is not, why would it need to be taught?
phrases.notes: If the spot didn't face the entrance, everyone already knows you can't slaughter there, so the ruling would add nothing.

phrases.english: Rather, even though
he slaughters opposite the entrance,
it teaches 'they may not slaughter' because the place is not holy;
so teach also: 'they are not liable.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13 and keeps the correction from Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case definition: the ruling must be about a case that adds something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Slaughter is banned only because the chamber does not face the entrance, so the chambers may be fully holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban covers even a chamber that faces the entrance, so its reason is lack of holiness. Therefore 'אין חייבין' is the right wording.
steps.whatToRemember: The chambers are holy by Torah law only for eating. For slaughter and for impurity liability they are not holy.

steps.title: Does eating also need to be opposite the entrance?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether eating קדשי קדשים also needs to be opposite the entrance. A ברייתא of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says two small doors were made to make the whole עזרה fit both for eating קדשי קדשים and for slaughtering קדשים קלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for eating, don't we need it to be opposite the entrance? But a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says there were two small doors in the בית החליפות, eight cubits high, to make the whole עזרה fit for eating קדשי קדשים and for slaughtering קדשים קלים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new difficulty. Until now it has assumed only slaughter must be opposite the entrance, and it brings a ברייתא suggesting that eating needs this too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 treated 'opposite the entrance' as a rule for slaughter alone. If eating also needs it, the chambers might have trouble with eating as well, which would clash with רבא's idea that they are holy for eating. The ברייתא says the small doors were made to fix both eating and slaughter, so it seems eating also needs 'opposite the entrance.'

keyTerms.meaning: Small doors or openings
A chamber in the מקדש (where knives were kept)
To make fit / valid
The Temple courtyard
Offerings of the highest holiness

phrases.english: And for eating, don't we need it to be opposite the entrance?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
There were two small doors in the Chamber of Knives,
their height was eight cubits;
in order to make the courtyard fit
for eating offerings of the highest holiness,
and for slaughtering offerings of lesser holiness!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about whether the 'opposite the entrance' rule also applies to eating
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that only slaughter, and not eating, must be opposite the entrance
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the small doors were needed to make the courtyard fit for eating too, so eating must also need to be opposite the entrance.

steps.title: רבינא removes 'eating' from the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers by taking the word 'eating' out of the ברייתא. The small doors were needed only for slaughtering קדשים קלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Remove 'eating' from here.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the challenge by fixing the wording of the ברייתא. The part about eating should not be there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 'eating' is removed, the ברייתא only says the doors made the courtyard fit for slaughter. So eating does not need to be opposite the entrance, and the earlier assumption stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Remove from here (take this out of the text)

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Remove 'eating' from here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that eating also needs to be opposite the entrance.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'eating' does not belong in the ברייתא. Only slaughter needs to be opposite the entrance.

steps.title: A פסוק seems to require eating at the entrance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבינא with a פסוק. משה told the כהנים to cook the meat at the entrance of the אהל מועד and eat it there, which suggests eating must be at the entrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'Cook the meat at the entrance of the אהל מועד, and eat it there'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבינא's removal of 'eating' with a פסוק that ties eating to the entrance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא said eating does not need to be opposite the entrance. The פסוק says 'and there you shall eat it,' meaning at the entrance of the אהל מועד. That seems to make the entrance a requirement for eating as well.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written?
The entrance of the Tent of Meeting

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכְתִיב: ״בַּשְּׁלוּ אֶת הַבָּשָׂר פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד,
phrases.english: But isn't it written: 'Cook the meat at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,
and eat it there'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכְתִיב: בַּשְּׁלוּ אֶת הַבָּשָׂר פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's answer in Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that eating does not need to be opposite the entrance
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק directly links eating to the entrance of the אהל מועד.

steps.title: Offerings for a one-time event are different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק speaks about the מילואים offerings, which were brought for one special time. We cannot learn general rules from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Offerings of a one-time occasion are different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the פסוק. That command was only for the special offerings of the מילואים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק was said about the offerings that inaugurated the משכן, which were never brought again. A command given for one special occasion does not set the rule for all offerings, so רבינא's position stands: eating does not need to be opposite the entrance.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings brought for a one-time occasion
Are different

steps.whatToRemember: Only slaughter of קדשים קלים needs to be opposite the entrance. Eating does not, and the פסוק about the מילואים was a one-time rule.

phrases.english: Offerings of a one-time occasion are different.
phrases.notes: This refers to the offerings of the משכן's inauguration in that פסוק; they were a one-time event.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the פסוק in Step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a special one-time case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק teaches that all offerings must be eaten at the entrance.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק was a special rule for the מילואים only, so in general eating does not need to be opposite the entrance.

steps.title: Blood becomes disqualified at sunset
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר אבודימי teaches that the דם of a קרבן becomes פסול at שקיעת החמה. He learns this from the פסוק 'ביום הקריבו את זבחו', reading it to mean that the blood is offered only on the day the animal was slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר אבודימי said: How do we know that the blood becomes unfit when the sun sets? Because the פסוק says, 'On the day he offers his זבח it shall be eaten.' This means: on the day you slaughter, you offer the blood. On a day you did not slaughter, you may not offer it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רב יצחק בר אבודימי gives a source from the תורה for the rule that the דם of a קרבן cannot be put on the מזבח after sunset.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links two things: 'הקריבו', offering, and 'זבחו', which he reads as slaughtering. So offering the blood is tied to the day of slaughter. Once the sun sets, that day is over, and the blood can no longer be offered.

keyTerms.meaning: Sunset, the end of the day.
Becomes unfit, so it can no longer be used for the קרבן.
His offering. The word comes from 'זביחה', slaughter.
Slaughters.
Offers. Here it means putting the blood on the מזבח.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic time limit for the עבודה of the blood. If the blood is not put on the מזבח on the day the animal was slaughtered, it can no longer be offered at all.

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Avudimi said:
From where do we know that the blood becomes disqualified
at sunset?
phrases.notes: After sunset, the blood can no longer be put on the מזבח.

phrases.english: As it says: 'On the day he offers'
his sacrifice, it shall be eaten'
on the day that you slaughter, you offer

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם שֶׁאִי אַתָּה זוֹבֵחַ אִי אַתָּה מַקְרִיב.
phrases.english: on a day that you do not slaughter, you do not offer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אֲבוּדִימִי: מִנַּיִן לְדָם שֶׁנִּפְסָל בִּשְׁקִיעַת הַחַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the מילואים ended in Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The דם of a קרבן becomes פסול at sunset. It may be offered only on the day the animal was slaughtered, as learned from 'ביום הקריבו את זבחו'.

steps.title: The verse is needed for something else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to challenge רב יצחק בר אבודימי. It says this פסוק is already needed for a different teaching. The rest of the challenge comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he needs this פסוק...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting to object that the פסוק is already used for another law. It says what that law is at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'הַאי מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ' means 'this is needed for' something else. The idea is that if the פסוק is already used to teach another law, it may not be free to teach the sunset rule too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He needs this', meaning this פסוק is already needed for a different teaching.

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence stops in the middle. The challenge is not finished here. The other use of the פסוק is given on the next amud.

phrases.english: But he needs this verse

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יצחק בר אבודימי's use of 'ביום הקריבו את זבחו' as the source for the sunset rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק that is already needed for one law cannot simply be used for another. The second use still has to be justified, and the next amud spells out the challenge.
